features.method: OpenStreetMap way 907808191, named 'ORNL Spallation Neutron Source' (amenity=research_institute), fetched via the Nominatim /lookup endpoint with polygon_geojson=1 (Overpass itself refused every connection attempt for most of this session; see the worklog's method note). Nodes kept verbatim, no simplification. This is the outer boundary of the whole SNS linac/ring/target complex, not a trace of Neutrino Alley itself: Neutrino Alley is a basement corridor inside the target building, somewhere within this ~0.7 x 1.4 km footprint, and no more specific public source or OSM element for it was found this session. Used here, honestly widened in `accuracy_m`, as the best available anchor for the detector-hosting site.

features.method: OpenStreetMap way 443660319 (building=yes, no name, 31 nodes, version 5, 2023-10-28T17:33:16Z) used verbatim: 6866 m2, largest extent 114 m. It is identified with ORNL building 8700 'Instrument Hall' by the same georeferencing as the linac record: ORNL's map polygon '8700 Instrument Hall' (92 vertices) transforms onto this footprint's position with a centroid offset of 30 m when 8700 is left out of the four-anchor fit (11 m when it is included), and its area transforms to about 5900 m2 against 6866 m2. ORNL's building text says 'Instrument Hall contains the SNS back-end system including the heavy-metal target, a vessel of liquid mercury, and 20 active beam lines'; so the target and the instruments are inside this footprint, but the target's own position within it is not sourced. Fit details: ORNL's interactive map (src:geo-ornl-interactive-map) has one map, 'Chestnut Ridge' (UMAP_2015071721664, 7000 x 4000 px), with seven labelled polygons: 8600 CLO, 8610 CNMS, 8630 JINS, 8640 Guest House, 8700 Instrument Hall, Second Target Station and 'SNS LINEAR Accelerator and Klystron Gallery'. The polygons are in the map's image units (x and y both scaled to the half-width). A similarity transform (rotation, uniform scale, translation, one mirror) from those units to metres was fitted by least squares to four pairs whose OSM footprints are identifiable by name or by size: the Guest House (OSM way 892578468, named 'ORNL Guest House', addr:housenumber 8640) and, by matching size and position, CLO to way 892578439, 8700 to way 443660319 and JINS to way 892578446. Fit: scale 673 m per image unit, rotation 18 deg, residual of the four anchors 9-13 m; leave-one-out predictions of an omitted anchor are 15-30 m off. Transforming the linac polygon with that fit puts its centroid 37 m (leave-one-out range 37-66 m) from the centroid of OSM way 892578460, with long axes at 20 and 28 deg and lengths along the axis of 403 m (ORNL polygon, hand-drawn, includes the klystron-gallery offsets) and 369 m (OSM). Way 892578460 is the only long thin building of the 25 in the SNS complex (the next longest, way 892578439, is 269 m in span but 8042 m2 in area, i.e. 30 m wide on average, and lies about 550 m east of where the ORNL polygon falls). The ORNL polygons were not copied; they only identify the OSM footprint.

ORNL's interactive map (src:geo-ornl-interactive-map) has one map, 'Chestnut Ridge' (UMAP_2015071721664, 7000 x 4000 px), with seven labelled polygons: 8600 CLO, 8610 CNMS, 8630 JINS, 8640 Guest House, 8700 Instrument Hall, Second Target Station and 'SNS LINEAR Accelerator and Klystron Gallery'. The polygons are in the map's image units (x and y both scaled to the half-width). A similarity transform (rotation, uniform scale, translation, one mirror) from those units to metres was fitted by least squares to four pairs whose OSM footprints are identifiable by name or by size: the Guest House (OSM way 892578468, named 'ORNL Guest House', addr:housenumber 8640) and, by matching size and position, CLO to way 892578439, 8700 to way 443660319 and JINS to way 892578446. Fit: scale 673 m per image unit, rotation 18 deg, residual of the four anchors 9-13 m; leave-one-out predictions of an omitted anchor are 15-30 m off. Transforming the linac polygon with that fit puts its centroid 37 m (leave-one-out range 37-66 m) from the centroid of OSM way 892578460, with long axes at 20 and 28 deg and lengths along the axis of 403 m (ORNL polygon, hand-drawn, includes the klystron-gallery offsets) and 369 m (OSM). Way 892578460 is the only long thin building of the 25 in the SNS complex (the next longest, way 892578439, is 269 m in span but 8042 m2 in area, i.e. 30 m wide on average, and lies about 550 m east of where the ORNL polygon falls). The ORNL polygons were not copied; they only identify the OSM footprint. What it is: the 'SNS LINEAR Accelerator and Klystron Gallery' of the ORNL map, i.e. the surface footprint of the klystron building together with the front-end building, with the berm-covered linac tunnel beside it; it is not the beam axis. Plausibility against sourced figures (not written as checks, because they are not like-for-like): the linac tunnel is 'The length of the linac tunnel is 1056 feet' (321.9 m), the klystron gallery '~330-m-long' (PAC 2001 and PAC 2003) and ORNL's 2005 news item 'the 1,000-foot linac' (src:geo-ornl-sns-cold-linac-2005), and the front-end building is a further '11000 square feet'; the footprint is 370 m long. The footprint's average width of 14.3 m compares with a klystron building 'width of 30 feet' (9.1 m) plus a tunnel '14' wide' (4.3 m) plus walls. Confidence stays approximate: OpenStreetMap alone, and an identification by georeferencing a hand-drawn polygon, not by a source that names the OSM building.

map.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Spallation Neutron Source

summary.plain: The Spallation Neutron Source at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Tennessee: the long linac building and the instrument hall that holds the mercury target are drawn at true scale inside the complex boundary. The accumulator ring and the two beam-transport lines are underground and have no published position, so they are listed as not located.

unlocated.backlog: A published SNS site or tunnel layout with a scale bar, coordinates or surveyed control points (the 1999 SNS EIS site plan, a civil-construction drawing set, or an IWAA/PAC survey paper giving ring-centre and linac-axis coordinates); georeference it against the linac structure and the 8700 hall drawn here (cite, never copy), then add length checks against 248.0 m (ring), 169 m (HEBT) and 151 m (RTBT). Do not draw the ring as a circle: it is a four-arc, four-straight-section lattice, and the layout figure in PAC 2003 TPPE011 is an unscaled schematic.
unlocated.reason: SNS accumulator ring (circumference 248.0 m), High Energy Beam Transport (169 m) and Ring-to-Target Beam Transport (151 m) lines. They are buried under the earth berm and are not mapped in OpenStreetMap (the complex holds only 25 building footprints, none of them a ring); ORNL's interactive map draws only the linac gallery, the Instrument Hall, CLO, CNMS, JINS and the Guest House; and the only layout figure found (PAC 2003 TPPE011, Fig. 1) is a labelled schematic without scale, coordinates or north. The derived distance from the linac end to the 8700 hall (about 220 m in this map) would not fix the ring's position, and the ring is a four-superperiod lattice, so no circle is drawn. The atlas has no accelerator record for the ring or the transfer lines (accelerator:sns is drawn through the linac structure).

unlocated.backlog: A COHERENT or SNS paper with a plan view of the target building basement and the alley (a scaled drawing or measured offsets from the target to each detector), or a basement drawing from ORNL; then place it from the 8700 footprint.
unlocated.reason: Neutrino Alley (the COHERENT detector corridor) and the target position. ORNL says the corridor is 50 m long and 'about 20 meters from the SNS target' at its closest point, and ORNL's map says the Instrument Hall (8700) 'contains the SNS back-end system including the heavy-metal target'; but no fetched source gives the target's position inside the 8700 footprint, the alley's bearing, or which building lies above it. The site is accounted for on the map by the complex boundary (drawn); the corridor and the COHERENT detectors are not drawn.
